text: Discovery is a shared mount plus a ccw peers tool (research fixes 1 and 3); not a shared pid namespace, not registry mirroring, not an HTTP relay.

Opt-in peers config section, disabled by default, zero behaviour change when off; keys enabled, dir (default /peers, same path in every container, socket path at most 103 bytes validated at config load), name (instance name, default hostname), probe_timeout_ms.

When enabled, per session: argv gets --messaging-socket-path <dir>/socks/<ccw session id>.sock; env gets CLAUDE_CODE_HARBOR_KITE=1 and CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_NAME=<instance>-<session name or id>; the ccw-written user settings.json gets crossSessionInbound: accept (only when enabled).

ccw creates <dir>/socks and <dir>/directory at startup with 0700 owned by the service uid, and refuses to start peers with a clear error if the dir is not ours or is group/world writable without the sticky bit, so Claude never silently falls back to /tmp/cc-socks-<uid>.

Peer directory: ccw writes <dir>/directory/<session id>.json atomically on session create {session_id, name, instance, address uds:<sock path>, cwd, started_at} and removes it on destroy and shutdown; liveness is an AF_UNIX connect probe with a timeout; sweeping stale entries whose socket refuses is allowed.

The ccw MCP server gets a second tool peers (no required params, optional instance filter) returning live peers excluding the caller, each with its uds address and a one-line SendMessage hint; registered only when peers.enabled; the agent instructions bootstrap gets a short paragraph about it when enabled.

The Dockerfile pre-creates /peers owned by agent (uid 1000) mode 0700 so a fresh named volume inherits ownership; a compose example runs two ccw services sharing one named peers volume mounted at /peers.

Tests use the fake claude only; only the fake-claude task edits tests/conftest.py; the fake claude accepts --messaging-socket-path and binds an AF_UNIX listener there; a docker-marked integration test starts two containers sharing a peers volume, creates a session in each via the API, and proves A's peers tool lists B and a connect from container A to B's socket succeeds; real-claude delivery is recorded as cannotVerify, not as a task.

README: setup, addressing, same-host-only limit (Unix sockets are kernel-local; Kubernetes needs pods on one node with a shared hostPath or RWX local volume), trust model (anything running as the agent uid with access to the dir can inject prompts into bypass-mode agents; the auth line is optional on Linux), config rows for every new key; examples config is a committed symlink into src/claude_code_wrapper/data/examples.
Follow the repo CLAUDE.md: test-first, uv run, plain ASCII, no em dashes.
